neighbours.label: The token right after an ordinal in an ordinal-led fixed phrase (second[-in]-command, Third[ Estate], 4th[ of] July, third[ through] fifth); cardinals and a free-standing ordinal are quiet. The - pole is the multiplicative side (double, triple, doubly)
fire: When the general fell ill, his second-in-command took charge of the siege.
The king summoned the nobles, the clergy and the Third Estate to Versailles.
The summer camp is open to children in second through eighth grade.
Fireworks lit the harbour on the 4th of July as the crowd cheered.
The gang leader was arrested, and his second-in-command fled across the border.
Newspapers were once proudly described as the Fourth Estate of the realm.
The tutoring scheme covers first through fourth year students at the college.
She was the third of seven daughters born to a village blacksmith.
quiet: When the general fell ill, his two commanders took charge of the siege.
The king summoned the nobles, the clergy and the merchants to Versailles.
The summer camp is open to children from eight to fourteen years old.
Fireworks lit the harbour in early July as the crowd cheered.
The gang leader was arrested, and his chief lieutenant fled across the border.
Newspapers were once proudly described as the watchdogs of the realm.
The tutoring scheme covers four hundred students at the college.
She was one of seven daughters born to a village blacksmith.

notes: Card: 'second[-in]-command' x2, 'third[ through] fifth', '4th[ of] July', 'Fourth[ Estate]', 'Third[ Estate]'. Probes: second-in-command 0.75, Third Estate 0.56, third through sixth 0.39, fifth of nine 0.31, 4th of July 0.27; two officers 0.01, early July 0.03, first class 0.02, 'third in the race' 0.15.
